results.content: === task instruction === # Date & time utilities: missing duration format, and the current output has drifted Our shared date & time utilities cover relative time, absolute time/date, and combined date-and-time/range formatting. Two things need fixing. ## 1. Add a duration format A duration format shows the absolute length of time (e.g. 2 seconds, 1 hour 30 minutes) — unlike relative time (e.g. "1 hour ago"). Add it alongside the existing formatters, following their conventions: an options object with `locale` and `style`, a sensible default style, exposed through the same public surface consumers already import from. Wrap the platform's native [`Intl.DurationFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DurationFormat). For 1 hour, 23 minutes and 45 seconds in `en-US`, the expected outputs are: | style | output | | --- | --- | | (default) | 1h 23m 45s | | long | 1 hour, 23 minutes, 45 seconds | | short | 1 hr, 23 min, 45 sec | | narrow | 1h 23m 45s | | digital | 1:23:45 | The attached design-guidance table defines these conventions (reference output, permitted variants, default per format) for the existing formatters — it has no Duration row yet; that's the gap this fills. ## 2. Fix the drift from that guidance Our internal demo pages, rendered against the current code, show several formatters — across more than one utility — no longer matching that guidance. The demos are self-checking: each row's caption states its own call/config, and the same value is shown across several locales side by side — so wrong output always sits next to a caption or locale column that shows what's right. Done when the duration format matches the table above, and everything in the demo screenshots renders the way the guidance table and each row's caption say it should. === task.toml === version = "1.0" [metadata] task_id = "carbon-design-system__carbon-22307-mm" title = "[Feature Request]: Date & Time format: Duration time format" repository_name = "carbon-design-system/carbon" repo_url = "https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon" issue_number = 22307 pr_number = 22313 base_commit = "217994d634aaffb2754b73e6dc85bcaaa629e8ff" fix_commit = "d7d92918bca89904e8fa413d1b3e5f3ef8c640b5" task_type = "visual_bug_fix" language = "TypeScript" framework = "none (framework-agnostic TypeScript utilities, Jest/jsdom harness)" cross_file = true visual_essentiality = "required" difficulty = "hard" difficulty_explanation = """ Two asks share one bundle, and a correct submission has to resolve both completely. 1. The upstream PR's own tests import the new module directly and never exercise the public barrel, so a synthetic f2p asserts the wiring explicitly - a fix that creates the module but forgets the barrel export does not score 1.0. 2. #                                    pass-through (all expectations derived from

STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt

REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }

# Paths come from the `diff --git` headers, not `+++ b/`: the latter is absent
# for binary, renamed and deleted entries. New-file paths (absent from
# harbor_base) fall through to `rm -f`, so vandalized copies are removed before
# test.patch recreates them.

    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do

  rm -f "/app/$_p.orig" "/app/$_p.rej" 2>/dev/null || true

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Verifier for carbon-design-system__carbon-22307-mm.

Reads the JUnit XML report produced by test.sh (jest-junit) and computes the
reward. NEVER inspects candidate source - reward derives solely from the test
report.

Reward domain is pass/fail only:
  1.0 - every f2p passes AND every p2p passes AND the rubric did not fail.
  0.0 - anything else. How close a partial fix got is carried by the counts.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P = CONF['f2p']
P2P = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'   # keep in sync with test.sh
REWARD_TXT = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
REWARD_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'

RUBRIC_NOT_GRADED = -1


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--rubric',
        default=None,
        help='Optional path to a rubric verdict file. Absent => rubric_passed = -1.',
    )
    args, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args()
    return args


def load_results():
    """Return {classname::name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as e:
        print(f'[verifier] XML parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        name = f"{tc.get('classname', '')}::{tc.get('name', '')}".strip(':')
        failed = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)
        results[name] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names (substring)."""

REWARD_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--rubric',
        default=None,
        help='Optional path to a rubric verdict file. Absent => rubric_passed = -1.',
    )
    args, _unknown = parser.parse_known_args()
    return args


def load_results():
    """Return {classname::name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as e:
        print(f'[verifier] XML parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        name = f"{tc.get('classname', '')}::{tc.get('name', '')}".strip(':')
        failed = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)
        results[name] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
    return results
